source.probe: advances from Word msgothic.ttc confirmed by a Word probe: Latin monospaced 0.5em

note:
MS Gothic family (Word-private on macOS, so the JA chain lands on Hiragino
Sans whose Latin is proportional and kana fullwidth). Advances measured from
Word's msgothic.ttc and confirmed by a Word probe (2026-09-03): MS Gothic
Latin is monospaced 0.5em; MS PGothic / MS UI Gothic have proportional kana
(frequency-weighted hiragana 0.900/0.776em, katakana 0.869/0.744em, long
vowel mark 0.961/0.816em), half-width brackets/colons, 0.664em ideographic
space/comma/period and Arial-class Latin at 0.9137x (space 1.0967x). Only
the ranges that differ from the Hiragino stand-in are claimed; kanji and the
fullwidth marks that stay 1em fall through to the chain. Latin-1 symbols the
real faces draw fullwidth (section/degree/plus-minus/multiply/divide...) come
from the bundled CJK subset where it has 1em glyphs and from the mono face
scaled up otherwise, since the chain's JA faces expose no Latin-1. The kana
and punctuation ranges live in separate "JA GO" families so a dual-slot run
keeps only the Latin alias in its ascii head and its eastAsia face still owns
the kana. Real faces (Windows) precede these aliases in the chain.
